newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakakibara sees no capital outflow on forex change.
newsitem.headline: Sakakibara sees no capital outflow on forex change.

text.p: Senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara told a parliamentary committee he does not see a capital outflow from Japan resulting from reform of foreign exchange rules passed by parliament on Friday.

"There is some misunderstanding that the revisions in the Foreign Exchange Control Law will trigger a capital outflow. It is not necessarily true that it will cause a capital outflow," said Sakakibara, head of the ministry's International Finance Bureau.
He said capital flow depends on factors such as currency risks and economic conditions both at home and abroad and movements in global interest rates.
There is a difference between capital outflow and financial transactions taking place overseas. "It seems that these are being confused," he said.
He added that he did not think that net capital transactions would change drastically in the short term.
